ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line AB and line CD intersect at point O, and OB bisects $\angle EOD$. If $\angle EOC = 110^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because \angle DOC = 180^\circ$ and $\angle EOC = 110^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle DOE = 180^\circ - \angle EOC = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ$, \\
Since $OB$ bisects $\angle EOD$, \\
$\therefore \angle BOD = \frac{1}{2} \angle DOE = \frac{1}{2} \times 70^\circ = \boxed{35^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, AB is a horizontal straight line passing through point O, A is on the left side, and B is on the right side. CD is an oblique straight line passing through point O, C is at the lower left, and D is at the upper right, so OC and OD are opposite rays. There is also a ray OE extending from O toward the lower right, and the rightward horizontal ray OB is located inside ∠EOD. Reasoning: The problem gives that OB bisects ∠EOD, and ∠EOC = 110°. Because OC and OD are opposite rays on the same straight line, ∠EOC and ∠EOD form a pair of linear angles, and their sum is 180°. Therefore ∠EOD = 180° - 110° = 70°. Also because OB bisects ∠EOD, ∠BOD = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.
